Authors: Guan X.; Zhao Z.
Title: LiteRE+: A Lightweight Embedding Relation Extraction Framework for Rapid Construction of Domain Knowledge Graphs
Source title: 2026 9th International Conference on Computer Information Science and Application Technology, CISAT 2026
Abstract: The task of relation extraction is an important part of constructing knowledge graphs. However, most of the current approaches are based on large-scale pre-trained language models, which are costly to train and challenging to implement in real-world, resource-constrained environments. In this paper, we present LiteRE+, a light-weight framework that combines hierarchical embeddings, a small Transformer encoder, and a dynamic negative sampling method to facilitate simultaneous extraction of entities and relations. The model is evaluated on the CoNLL04 dataset. Experimental results show that LiteRE+ achieves a relation extraction F1-score of 74.21%. Compared with SpERT, LiteRE+ reduces the training time per epoch from 8.5 min to 4.2 min and lowers peak GPU memory usage from 4.2 GB to 2.8 GB, corresponding to approximately a 2.0× speedup and a 33% reduction in memory consumption. These results demonstrate that a carefully designed lightweight architecture can maintain competitive extraction performance while substantially improving computational efficiency.  © 2026 IEEE.

Authors: Li Y.; Wang Y.; Wang H.; Yan Y.; Yang F.; Pan Z.; Tong Z.; Li Y.; Wu W.; Jiang B.; Bai M.; Xie Y.; Zhou Y.; Zhu F.
Title: Empowering LLMs for biomedical information extraction with RAG-ICL and DFPO
Source title: Pattern Recognition
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities for biomedical information extraction (IE), but their application to named entity recognition (NER) and relation extraction (RE) remains limited by prototype selection, preference alignment, and structured-output validity. In this study, we formulate LLM-based biomedical IE as a structure-constrained pattern recognition problem and propose a framework centered on two complementary adaptation mechanisms. Retrieval-Augmented In-Context Learning (RAG-ICL) performs inference-time prototype selection by retrieving and reranking instance-specific demonstrations, enabling LLMs to use more relevant contextual examples without parameter updates. Dual-Phase Fine-tuning with Preference Optimization (DFPO) performs training-time parameter alignment through supervised fine-tuning, MFPEA-based structured preference data, DPO-Positive optimization, and post-finetuning. In addition, Dual-Mode Correction and Review (DMCR) is used as an auxiliary output-side verification module to improve parsability and reduce malformed structured predictions. Experiments across biomedical NER and RE benchmarks show that RAG-ICL improves over zero-shot and random/fixed ICL baselines, while DFPO consistently enhances extraction performance over supervised fine-tuning and representative biomedical IE systems. Further analyses demonstrate the importance of compact, relevant demonstrations, the incremental contribution of DFPO stages, and the practical trade-off between inference-time and training-time adaptation. These results suggest that decomposing LLM-based biomedical IE into prototype selection, preference-aware decision alignment, and structural verification provides an effective and coherent framework for schema-constrained biomedical text recognition. © 2026

Authors: Kokare R.; Mane S.
Title: LoRA based instruction fine tuning of large language models for agronomic triple extraction and GraphRAG knowledge retrieval
Source title: Discover Artificial Intelligence
Abstract: Due to massive growth in the unstructured agricultural data generated from reports, research articles, news, farmers’ feedback, experts’ advice, etc, there is a need to utilize this information efficiently for knowledge representation and decision-making. There are multiple techniques where information extraction and managing it in a structured manner can be less challenging. LLMs are used widely for extracting meaningful information in the way the user instructs. More precisely, LLMs, when fine-tuned on domain-specific data, e.g, agricultural data, help to retrieve information promptly. We propose a framework where the Llama model is fine-tuned using the LoRA technique and an instruction dataset for extracting triplets from the unstructured agronomic data. Further, this Llama-LoRA-based model is used to generate knowledge, which will efficiently help to retrieve the query results for the user using GraphRAG. Domain-specific instructional fine-tuning has shown a significant rise in performance. ROUGE and BLEU precision results of the proposed framework have outperformed the response retrieval compared to other retrieval techniques. Proposed results of domain-specific instructional fine-tuned Llama-LoRA model have overcome the limitations of knowledge representation and unstructured data extraction through GraphRAG, resulting in semantic search with contextual retrieval. © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Zhang X.; Pan H.; Huang J.; Jiang H.; Ye H.; Wu X.; Zhang D.; Wang P.; Wang B.
Title: AURORA-RE: Reinforcement Learning-Enhanced Document-Level Relation Extraction with Large Language Models
Source title: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
Abstract: Document-level relation extraction with general-purpose large language models suffers from evaluation–training mismatch, weak domain adaptation, and scarce high-quality labels in industry texts. While extremely large models improve F1, they impose prohibitive memory and computational costs for resource-constrained deployment. To address these challenges, we propose a training method combining data construction, full-parameter supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning with custom reward functions to directly align evaluation objectives with training signals, abbreviated as AURORA-RE. First, we design three reward functions: Triplet-Set F1 Reward optimizes set-level precision, recall, and F1 to bridge the gap between token-level loss and triplet-level metrics; Similarity-Weighted Reward constrains cross-sentence and multi-hop reasoning chains using Jaccard similarity, coverage, and length matching; Format Compliance Reward ensures structured parsing requirements. Second, we establish a closed-loop process of data annotation, full-parameter alignment, and reward optimization with GRPO to improve cross-sentence and multi-hop extraction on smaller-scale models. Third, we design multi-level data screening and quality control with semi-automatic annotation and rule filtering for scalable corpus construction. On industry economic news data, our method achieves 33.50% F1, significantly outperforming the same-scale base model (10.14%) and a four-times-larger model (28.97%). On Re-DocRED, F1 improves from 2.75% to 41.67%. These results demonstrate that our method significantly improves performance while reducing deployment costs, validating the effectiveness of custom reward-based LLM training for document-level relation extraction. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: Ranking-Guided Autoregressive Modeling for Multimodal Tabular Anomaly Detection
Source title: CEUR Workshop Proceedings
Abstract: Tabular data on the Web is frequently heterogeneous, multimodal, and published in a decentralised way, making it prone to structural and semantic inconsistencies. As such datasets increasingly serve as sources for knowledge graph construction, ensuring structural and semantic consistency prior to integration becomes critical. One approach to dealing with these issues is anomaly detection, a technique that identifies irregular patterns in a given dataset. Although several approaches exist for anomaly detection on tables, methods that capture interactions between different modalities, rather than treating each modality separately, are rare. This paper begins to address this gap by introducing a new Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) architecture designed for anomaly detection on multimodal tabular datasets. By combining a dual objective that is comprised of an autoregressive and a pairwise ranking loss, the model is able to efficiently learn both patterns of textual and visual data and understand cross-modal correlations. Experimental results show a performance gain of 58.4% for our architecture on a diverse set of anomaly categories. Authors: Zheng R.; Xu J.
Title: A Synergized LLM-KG Framework for Domain Knowledge Cognition
Source title: Proceedings of the International Symposium on Automation and Robotics in Construction
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) evolve rapidly, yet their probabilistic generation is inherently non-traceable and leaves a persistent bottleneck in domain knowledge cognition. Retrieval augmentation via texts or knowledge-graphs (KGs) improves coverage and factual accuracy, but existing studies still depend largely on static knowledge structures and manually governed updating, so the obstacle to sustained and reliable domain knowledge cognition remains. This study therefore proposes a synergized LLM-KG framework for domain knowledge, centered on ontology-governed KG automatic generation (AutoGen) and update, and hybrid vector-graph retrieval for clause-grounded reasoning. Specifically, guided by a manually developed ontology, the KG is automatically constructed, incrementally enriched, and jointly used with vector retrieval to ground each query against both textual evidence and graph structure. A case study is conducted in construction contract management. Results demonstrate the robust KG AutoGen performance with average F1 scores of 0.904 for entity extraction and 0.856 for triple extraction. Across three query stages, the framework further improves multi-hop reasoning and clause-grounded accuracy, with its F1 advantage over GraphRAG widening from 0.00 to 0.37 and that over LLM-only prompting increasing from 0.25 to 0.45. This study provides a traceable route to deeper, more reliable, and continually refined domain knowledge cognition. © 2026 International Association on Automation and Robotics in Construction. Title: AI-Powered Medical Report Analyzer and Organ Visualization
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: This article describes a medical insights engine powered by artificial intelligence that utilizes natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision to decipher clinically meaningful content from unstructured medical transcriptions and radiological images. The system integrates biomedical Named Entity Recognition (NER), relation extraction, anatomical visualization, and temporal disease tracking using vision–language models. A Streamlit interface combines RAG-based clinical question answering and LLM-driven summarization. Experiments on medical transcripts, NIH ChestX-ray14, and biomedical ontologies achieved an F1-score of 0.91 for NER, 0.88 for relation extraction, and a BLEU score of 0.67 for image captioning. The framework demonstrates improved multimodal interpretability and unified clinical diagnostics. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Title: Design of an Intelligent Question-Answering Model for Family Traditions and Precepts Integrating Knowledge Graph and Large Language Model
Source title: Proceedings of 2026 3rd Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area International Conference on Digital Economy and Artificial Intelligence, DEAI 2026
Abstract: This paper designs an intelligent question-answering model for family traditions and precepts that integrates Knowledge Graph (KG) and Large Language Model (LLM), aiming to address the problems of fragmented knowledge, insufficient semantic understanding, high answer illusion rate, and lack of emotional adaptation in existing systems. The model adopts a hierarchical collaborative architecture, including four modules: user interaction, knowledge graph construction, KG-LLM-EKA fusion algorithm, question-answer generation, and optimization. A family traditions and precepts knowledge graph covering 6 ethical dimensions, 1200+ entities, and 5000+ triples is constructed. The KG-LLM-EKA algorithm is proposed, achieving deep integration of KG and LLM through emotional weight annotation, dynamic knowledge alignment, collaborative generation, and illusion suppression mechanisms. Experimental results show that the model achieves an F1 score of 89.7%, an accuracy of 88.3%, and an illusion rate of only 3.2% on the self-built test set and supplementary validation set, with an average user satisfaction score of 4.2. All indicators are superior to comparative models such as pure LLM and KG-Adapter. This model effectively improves the accuracy and emotional relevance of family tradition and precept question-and-answer sessions, providing technical support for the intelligent dissemination of family tradition and precepts and the digital inheritance of traditional culture. © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

Title: Construction of a Knowledge Graph for Functional Specification Standards of Traditional Chinese Medicine Information Systems Based on Large Language Models
Source title: Proceedings of 2026 2nd International Conference on Health Big Data, HBD 2026
Abstract: Objective: To address the issue of fragmented knowledge in functional specification documents for Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) information systems and enable the querying and improve the readability of standard knowledge. Methods: Using 22 functional specification standard documents related to TCM information systems from the group standards issued by the China Association of Chinese Medicine Informatics as the data source, we designed domain-constrained prompts based on the CRISPE framework to guide the DeepSeek large language model in extracting entities and relations. We then integrated rule-based constraints to construct the knowledge graph. Results: A knowledge graph consisting of 2294 nodes and 6330 relations was generated. The graph structure is clear and semantically consistent, capable of efficiently supporting queries and visualization. Authors: Li S.; Tian C.; Du X.; Li Y.
Title: Forecasting secondary risks in emergencies: A transferable early warning framework using event logic graphs from social media
Source title: Information Processing and Management
Abstract: Social media has become a critical arena for public opinion during emergencies, where the rapid evolution of events can generate unforeseen secondary risks. This study develops and validates a transferable early warning framework that applies Event Logic Graphs (ELGs) to move beyond retrospective analysis, toward proactive risk forecasting. First, this study proposes a novel hybrid Rule-Large Language Model framework to extract events and multiple types of logical relations from noisy social media data. Second, a comparative analysis is conducted by constructing separate ELGs for each event: a natural disaster and public health crisis. Finally, regarding the historical ELG as the knowledge base, the framework incorporates the event chain similarity calculations with context-aware filtering and sentiment enhanced re-ranking mechanism. Specifically, this mechanism ensures prediction validity by filtering context mismatched risks and capturing verified public sentiment to prioritize potential threats. The results present that the hybrid framework significantly outperforms the pure rule-based model in logic triples extraction. The analysis reveals that emergencies evolve into two different structural prototypes: natural disaster is manifested as “linear cascade” models, and public health crisis shows “cyclic feedback loop” characteristics, which provides a new computational perspective for agenda setting theory. In addition, the cross-event secondary risk prediction framework achieves satisfactory predictive performance across Top-3, 5, and 10 cutoffs, demonstrating that integrating context constraints and, more critically, credibility weighted sentiment analysis, achieves the most substantial improvement in identifying high-priority risks. This research contributes to the literature by proposing a robust method for building ELG with multiple logical relationships, helping emergency management shift from passive monitoring to active risk prevention and control. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: MED-KG-LLM: A Modular Pipeline for Knowledge Graph–Augmented Medical Question Answering on Clinical Data
Source title: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
Abstract: With the growing digitization of electronic health records (EHRs), there is an urgent need to transform raw, unstructured clinical tabular data into structured representations that support accurate and explainable question answering (QA). We introduce MED-KG-LLM, a fully modular and scalable pipeline that ingests raw dataset based patient-symptom records, performs hybrid named entity recognition (NER) using spaCy and BioBERT, and applies deterministic pattern-driven open information extraction to produce normalized subject-predicate-object triples. These triples populate a multi-view biomedical knowledge graph (KG) in NetworkX, partitioned by relation type (e.g., treatment, symptom association, contraindication). For query processing, both user questions and KG components are embedded with a proprietary OpenAI model; relevant graph passages are retrieved via approximate nearest neighbor search. A two-stage answer generation cascade first leverages BioGPT for domain-specific draft responses, followed by GPT-4o-mini for fluency and factual refinement. We evaluate our system on three publicly available healthcare datasets, benchmarking generated answers against human ground truths using BERTScore, ROUGE-L, and METEOR. Experimental results demonstrate that MED-KG-LLM substantially outperforms existing baselines (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, DeepSeek) in both semantic accuracy and linguistic quality, highlighting its potential as an end-to-end solution for clinical QA over tabular medical data. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Authors: Zou Y.; Wang S.; Li G.; Ning B.
Title: MaRAG: a knowledge graph and retrieval-augmented framework for maritime accident analysis
Source title: Ocean Engineering
Abstract: Maritime transportation underpins global trade and energy supply, however, growing fleet sizes, complex vessel systems, and evolving regulatory and environmental pressures necessitate more intelligent approaches to accident prevention, response, and analysis. Traditional knowledge management systems-reliant on expert experience and static databases-struggle with heterogeneous data, temporal-causal dynamics, and cross-disciplinary integration. Existing data-driven methods often lack structural grounding, reasoning-aware querying, and result traceability. To address these gaps, we propose MaRAG, a multi-agent framework that defines a new form of knowledge representation through a hierarchical, cascade-enhanced ontology and co-designs tailored retrieval and inference workflows. MaRAG integrates ontology-guided knowledge graph construction, Optimal Transport-based feature alignment, dual-database storage, and an intelligent, multi-paradigm retrieval mechanism. Experiments and case studies show that MaRAG significantly outperforms LLM- and RAG-based baselines in maritime accident Question-Answering and causal reasoning, achieving higher Exact Match, Precision, and F1 scores across varying knowledge graph scales. Analyses confirm its ability to reduce knowledge fragmentation and deliver a scalable, interpretable system for maritime safety decision-making. © 2025 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Towards a Meta-Model for Integrating Knowledge Graph Extraction Into LLM-Enhanced Engineering Design
Source title: Proceedings of the IEEE National Aerospace Electronics Conference, NAECON
Abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) tools, specifically LLMs, have seen an explosion in use across professional fields in recent years. Researchers have explored integrating GenAI tools into Multi Agent Systems (MAS) for automated engineering design pipelines. However, engineering subfields contain domain knowledge which includes tacit expertise that is often missing from LLM training data. Applying LLMs without tacit knowledge to domain-specific tasks increases the risk of injecting false or misguided information into the design process. These risks are even further amplified when using autonomous Agentic LLMs that can act independently. Knowledge Graphs (KGs) can improve LLM behavior, but manual domain KG creation is resource intensive. Automating KG creation via Knowledge Graph Extraction (KGE) using LLMs is becoming more common, but its implementation is underexplored in engineering design pipelines. This paper proposes a meta model to explore the tradespace behind LLM-based options for MAS engineering design workflows. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Integrating knowledge graphs and LLMs for intelligent full-chain safety risk pre-control in large hydropower projects
Source title: Automation in Construction
Abstract: Construction safety risks (CSRs) in large hydropower projects (LHPs) are difficult to manage due to complex interactions, dynamic evolution, and cascading propagation. This paper investigates how to achieve intelligent CSR knowledge modeling and proactive risk pre-control for LHP construction. An intelligent framework is developed by integrating ALBERT-BiLSTM-Att-CRF-based entity recognition, association-rule-based relation extraction, knowledge graph (KG) construction, and large language model (LLM)-enhanced decision support. The results show that the proposed framework effectively identifies CSR entities (F1 > 90%), multi-hop risk propagation paths, and supports accurate knowledge retrieval and intelligent pre-control recommendations (overall closed-ended question-answering accuracy of 0.8667 and an expert relevance score of 4.21/5.00 for open-ended recommendations). This study provides an interpretable and scalable solution for safety managers and engineers to enhance risk identification and decision-making in complex engineering projects. The findings inspire future research on integrating multimodal data and advanced artificial intelligence techniques for more adaptive construction safety management. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Forer L.; Hope T.
Title: Inferring Scientific Cross-Document Coreference and Hierarchy with Definition-Augmented Relational Reasoning
Source title: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
Abstract: We address the fundamental task of inferring cross-document coreference and hierarchy in scientific texts, which has important applications in knowledge graph construction, search, recommendation and discovery. Large Language Models (LLMs) can struggle when faced with many long-tail technical concepts with nuanced variations. We present a novel method which generates context-dependent definitions of concept mentions by retrieving full-text literature, and uses the definitions to enhance detection of cross-document relations. We further generate relational definitions, which describe how two concept mentions are related or different, and design an efficient re-ranking approach to address the combinatorial explosion involved in inferring links across papers. In both fine-tuning and in-context learning settings, we achieve large gains in performance on data subsets with high amount of different surfaces forms and ambiguity, that are challenging for models. We provide analysis of generated definitions, shedding light on the relational reasoning ability of LLMs over fine-grained scientific concepts. © 2026 Association for Computational Linguistics. Title: Context Graph: Conversational State Tracking for Knowledge Graph Construction
Source title: Proceedings of 9th International Conference on Inventive Computation Technologies, ICICT 2026
Abstract: The volume of new medical research is growing too fast for humans to read and organize manually. To solve this, researchers use Knowledge Graphs (KGs) to turn text into structured data (connecting drugs, diseases, and proteins). However, existing computer programs struggle to read complex medical text because they often process one sentence at a time, forgetting the context. The primary objective of this study is to introduce Context Graph, a novel Conversational State Tracking system that resolves implicit entity references by treating the reading process as a stateful conversation with a Large Language Model (GPT-4o). To ensure data fidelity, we enforce strict structural validation via Pydantic and standardize entities using the Unified Medical Language System (UMLS). Key findings demonstrate that Context Graph achieves a state-of-the-art accuracy of 74.92% on the MINE benchmark, significantly outperforming the previous best method (KGGen at 66.07%). Authors: Lu Y.; Zhan J.; Chen J.
Title: EvoMod: Evolutionary Optimization of Modular Prompts for Biomedical Relation Extraction
Source title: ACM-BCB 2026 - 17th ACM International Conference on Bioinformatics, Computational Biology and Health Informatics
Abstract: Biomedical relation extraction (RE) with large language models involves numerous interacting prompt concerns - from reasoning strategy and domain knowledge to exemplar selection, among others - yet no automatic prompt optimization (APO) framework has been developed specifically for biomedical RE, leaving prompt engineering manual and dataset-specific for the community. General-purpose APO methods treat the prompt as a monolithic unit, preventing attribution of performance to individual components and limiting interpretability. We present EvoMod, a modular APO framework for biomedical RE that decomposes prompts into typed functional modules, enabling independent optimization and attribution of each component's contribution. A three-phase pipeline, preceded by a preliminary Phase 0 that generates LLM-produced label descriptions as a base prompt, initializes modules with Lamarckian seeds grounded in the model's own error patterns and evolves each through error gradient descent with role-constrained validation (Phase 1), optimizes in-context exemplars via contrastive-diverse selection (Phase 2), and composes the best module subset via beam search with order optimization (Phase 3). We evaluate on five biomedical RE benchmarks spanning protein, gene, chemical, drug, and disease entity pairs across three open-weight LLMs ranging from 4B to 120B parameters. EvoMod achieves consistent improvements over zero-shot baselines and state-of-the-art APO methods, with up to +0.15 micro-F1 over the next-best baseline on DDI and +0.13 on ChemProt. © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

Authors: Wu L.; Xia X.; Wan Y.; Li R.; Yin X.; Chen L.; Ju S.
Title: Construction of a Dynamic Depression Knowledge Graph Based on Multi-source Heterogeneous Data Fusion; [基于多源异构数据融合的动态抑郁症知识图谱构建]
Source title: Gongcheng Kexue Yu Jishu/Advanced Engineering Sciences
Abstract: Objective Depression, recognized as the most disabling mental disorder globally, presents significant challenges to the development and maintenance of depression knowledge bases. Its complex multi-target treatment mechanisms and the continuously expanding body of medical literature require both high domain specificity and timely updates in these knowledge bases. Currently, the construction and application of depression knowledge graphs face three critical bottlenecks. The first is delayed knowledge updating, which makes it difficult for knowledge graphs to keep pace with the latest research findings and clinical practices in the field of depression. The second is the insufficient domain adaptability of relation extraction, as existing methods often fail to accurately identify and extract the fine-grained semantic relationships specific to depression-related entities. The third is semantic conflict among multi-source data, arising from the heterogeneous structures and semantics of different depression-related data sources. Therefore, this study proposes a novel method for constructing a dynamic depression knowledge graph based on multi-source heterogeneous data fusion. Methods The proposed method began with the integration of various heterogeneous depression-related data sources. It comprehensively combined the ICD-11 clinical diagnostic criteria, DrugBank drug data, the PubMed literature database, and domestic and international medical guidelines. A depression domain ontology was constructed with four core categories: diseases, drugs, symptoms, and non-pharmacological treatment methods, establishing a foundation for semantic consistency. A two-stage strategy was employed to address domain adaptability issues in relation extraction. First, pre-training on structured knowledge bases was conducted to provide the model with a general understanding of semantic relationships associated with depression-related knowledge. The model was then fine-tuned using depression medical relation extraction datasets. In addition, a chain of thought reasoning mechanism was introduced to enhance the model's reasoning and comprehension of complex semantic relationships among depression-related entities. An incremental triple-generation framework based on large language models was designed to address the challenge of delayed knowledge updates. The dynamic update module within this framework played a critical role by supporting the real-time integration of new evidence identified from the latest research findings and clinical practices. In addition, it enabled PMID tracing, allowing convenient verification of the sources of newly incorporated knowledge. An ontology-driven multi-source heterogeneous data fusion mechanism was established. This mechanism effectively resolved semantic expression conflicts between structured data, such as information from drug databases, and unstructured literature from academic publications, ensuring their consistent integration into the knowledge graph. The overall architecture formed a closed-loop system through a dynamic feedback mechanism. When new evidence emerged, it was first processed by the extraction enhancement layer to identify relevant information. Then, the dynamic update layer integrated the new information while considering its timeliness. Finally, the semantic fusion layer performed consistency verification against the existing knowledge system, ensuring the integrity and accuracy of the knowledge graph. Results and Discussions In the experimental evaluation, the performance of the relation extraction model was assessed from multiple perspectives. The fine-tuning performance of the model was compared to several baseline models, including medical pre-trained language models, fine-tuned lightweight large models in the medical domain, and general large models (GPT-4o and DeepSeek). The superiority of the proposed domain-adaptive relation extraction model was first demonstrated through fine-tuning experiments, in which its performance exceeded that of all competing models across three benchmark datasets. Specifically, it achieved an accuracy of 95.20 on the ChemProt dataset and 91.42 on the DDI dataset. In addition, its F1 score on the DDI dataset was 1.67 to 5.42 higher than that of competing models. Compared to the base model Llama-3.1-8 B-Instruct, the F1 score on the RE dataset increased by 13.78, strongly validating the domain generalization capability of the proposed method. In the few-shot learning scenarios of the RE-5-shot and ChemProt-5-shot tasks, the proposed model outperformed large-scale general models such as GPT-4o and DeepSeek. On the RE-5-shot dataset, the F1 score of the proposed method increased by 35.2 to 43.6 compared to that of the general models. On the ChemProt-5-shot dataset, the F1 score improved by 15.5 to 23.6. These findings indicated that the fine-tuned relation extraction model more accurately recognized the biomedical relation types defined in this study. In the expert evaluation experiment, experts with extensive experience in depression research and clinical practice were invited to assess the constructed depression knowledge graph. The evaluation results showed that the depression knowledge graph achieved an accuracy of 92.1, indicating a high level of quality in terms of accuracy and professional reliability. In addition, continuous monitoring throughout the knowledge integration process revealed that the model maintained stable processing efficiency through the dynamic update mechanism. Conclusions The method for constructing a dynamic depression knowledge graph based on multi-source heterogeneous data fusion, as proposed in this study, provides scalable and dynamic support for mental disorder knowledge management. It effectively addresses the three major bottlenecks encountered by current depression knowledge graphs and demonstrates excellent performance across multiple evaluation aspects. This methodology has significant reference value for the construction of knowledge graphs related to other complex diseases. In addition, it provides a high-quality knowledge base for developing depression diagnosis and treatment systems. Future research will focus on integrating knowledge graphs with large language models to reduce model hallucinations through retrieval-enhanced generation, assist primary care physicians in making more accurate diagnoses, and provide personalized diagnostic and treatment recommendations for patients with depression. © 2026, Sichuan University. Title: A Scalable Method for Validated Data Extraction from Electronic Health Records with Large Language Models
Source title: AI in Precision Oncology
Abstract: Purpose/Background: Health care organizations increasingly require structured, patient-level clinical variables for treatment decisions, operational workflows, quality measurement, and clinical trial screening. Relevant information is often fragmented across heterogeneous electronic health record (EHR) systems, unstructured formats, and scanned documents. Large language models (LLMs) offer an opportunity to enhance medical record extraction, particularly in oncology where point-of-care structured coding rarely captures a patient’s full longitudinal clinical course. Methods: Two complementary LLM-based approaches were developed. The first performed schema-based Named Entity Recognition and Relation Extraction from unstructured documents, normalizing outputs to Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources and Observational Health Data Sciences and Informatics vocabularies. The second used a retrieval-augmented checklist framework that queried embedded document text alongside structured data, returning custom outputs with evidence-based justifications and source citations. Performance was evaluated through human validation, automated consistency checks, and iterative error analysis. Results: Schema-based LLM extractors for medications, radiation, and surgical procedures achieved ∼95% accuracy, precision, recall, and F1. Deployed across 3,493 patients, LLM extraction yielded a 207% increase in distinct oncology drug ingredients over structured EHR sources. Oncology therapies were captured for 65% of patients versus 40% in structured data, with dramatically improved attribute coverage: indication for prescription (71% vs. 5%) and reason for discontinuation (10% vs. 0%). For radiation and oncology surgical procedures, LLM extraction yielded more than triple the patient coverage versus structured sources. The checklist framework achieved strong F1 scores in extracting cancer diagnosis variables (99.0%) and lines of therapy (97.6%) across 4,802 validated elements. Cancer diagnoses and dates were identified for 93.5% of patients versus 69.8% in structured data; stage and grade were extracted for 64% and 62% versus near-zero structured availability. A lines-of-therapy checklist generated 4,218 treatment lines across 2,320 patients, capturing regimen dates, best response, discontinuation reasons, and progression dates. Among patients with response data, objective response rate declined from 65% at first line to 22% at third line, with first-line response rates ranging from 43% in colorectal to 85% in esophageal cancer. Conclusions: Two complementary LLM-based strategies substantially enhanced the completeness and utility of structured clinical data from heterogeneous medical records, supporting scalable generation of interoperable patient-level datasets for clinical analytics, research, and operational workflows. © The Author(s) 2026. Title: SynEL: A synthetic benchmark for entity linking
Source title: PLOS ONE
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) offer significant potential for constructing commonsense knowledge graphs from text, demonstrating adaptability across diverse domains. However, their effectiveness varies significantly with domain-specific language, highlighting a critical need for specialized benchmarks to assess and optimize knowledge graph construction sub-tasks like named entity recognition, relation extraction, and entity linking. Currently, domain-specific benchmarks are scarce. To address this gap, we introduce SynEL, a novel benchmark developed for evaluating text-based knowledge extraction methods, validated using customer support dialogues. We present a comprehensive methodology for benchmark construction, propose two distinct approaches for generating synthetic datasets, and evaluate accumulated hallucinations. Title: Knowledge-Enhanced Image Captioning with Adaptive Graph-based Multimodal Alignment and LLM
Source title: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
Abstract: Image captioning is crucial for multimodal understanding, bridging visual content and natural language. Despite recent advancements in Large Multimodal Models (LMMs), when faced with unseen entities or scenes in the open world, even when attempting to leverage learned knowledge, models still struggle with vague and inaccurate descriptions, and may even generate knowledge hallucinations. A key reason is that the model fails to effectively integrate knowledge with visual information, limiting its understanding of visual content. Thus, we propose Adaptive Knowledge Graph-guided Multimodal Alignment (AKGMA) for image captioning, which enhances semantic understanding in open-world scenes through visual knowledge reasoning, reducing knowledge hallucinations and improving caption quality. It consist three key components: Entity-guided Knowledge Aligner (EKA), Adaptive Knowledge Graph Construction (AKGC), and Scene-Context Knowledge Adapter (SCKA). EKA connects visual entities to knowledge graphs, providing structured knowledge to a small language model, which interacts with a visual encoder to acquire visual knowledge. AKGC uses reinforcement learning to build image-relevant subgraphs to optimize knowledge prompts and improve knowledge hallucinations. SCKA leverages scene graph annotations to extract visual contextual knowledge and inject it into Large Language Models (LLMs), ensuring the generated descriptions are consistent with the image’s details. Additionally, we introduce UniKnowCap, a new image knowledge description dataset spanning various open-world knowledge domains, designed to evaluate the knowledge accuracy and detail consistency of model-generated descriptions. Extensive experiments show our model outperforms baselines across multiple metrics. © 2026, Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (www.aaai.org). All rights reserved.

Title: KGSR-WaterNet: A knowledge-driven framework for multi-indicator water quality prediction via signed relation modeling

Abstract: To address the limited use of water-environment knowledge and the difficulty of modeling facilitating and inhibitory relationships among indicators, this study proposes KGSR-WaterNet, a knowledge-driven framework for multi-indicator water quality prediction via signed relation modeling. Title: Consistency–accuracy correlation in hard-prompted LLMs for entity and relation extraction: empirical findings from plant-health data
Source title: Genomics and Informatics
Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) become increasingly popular for information extraction (IE), concerns persist regarding the stability and reliability of their outputs. While accuracy has traditionally been the main evaluation metric, consistency—defined as the stability of model outputs across repeated runs—has recently been proposed as a complementary signal of reliability. In this work, we examine the relationship between accuracy and consistency in hard-prompted generative LLMs applied to entity and relation extraction. We conduct a systematic evaluation using four LLMs (GPT, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi) on the EPOP corpus, a plant-health dataset with rich entity types, long-range relations, overlapping relations, and strong argument constraints. To refine the interpretation of consistency, we distinguish between recoverable output variations—those that preserve the meaning of the extracted information—and critical ones that result in semantic errors. Our results show that while some positive correlation between accuracy and consistency exists, it is model-dependent and varies with task complexity. In structured prediction tasks, we show that consistency should be measured at the semantic level, ignoring superficial variations in format or wording. These insights have important implications for using self-consistency as a confidence filter and for designing reliable generative IE pipelines in specialized domains. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Few-shot and chain-of-thought prompting for equipment maintenance knowledge graph construction via large language models
Source title: Knowledge-Based Systems
Abstract: Equipment operation and maintenance (O&M) is fundamental for ensuring the normal operation of equipment, and the accumulation and reuse of knowledge are critical supports for efficient O&M. Knowledge Graphs (KGs), as advanced tools for knowledge storage and management, facilitate intricate knowledge association queries and rapid issue localization, thereby substantially enhancing operational efficiency. However, traditional KG construction methods face limitations such as heavy reliance on extensive manual data annotation, inadequate contextual understanding, and low accuracy in extracting complex relations. To address these challenges, this paper proposes FSCoT-EMKG: a method combining few-shot learning and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting with large language models (LLMs) for constructing KGs in the domain of equipment O&M. This approach integrates CoT and few-shot learning examples into prompts and incorporates relation ontology to enhance LLMs' capabilities in performing high-quality knowledge extraction tasks, thus optimizing KG construction processes. The method assigns the role of knowledge extraction experts to LLMs, clearly defining their responsibilities within the task. Title: TAdaRAG: Task Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation via On-the-Fly Knowledge Graph Construction
Source title: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
Abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) improves large language models by retrieving external knowledge, often truncated into smaller chunks due to the input context window, which leads to information loss, resulting in response hallucinations and broken reasoning chains. Title: HERTy-Wiki: A Benchmark for Hierarchical Entity Reasoning and Typing in Wikidata
Source title: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
Abstract: Entity typing is central to knowledge engineering, and as large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support knowledge graph construction, it becomes essential to assess how reliably they can perform this task. We present HERTy-Wiki (Hierarchical Entity Reasoning and Typing in Wikidata) - a human-verified benchmark for evaluating hierarchical reasoning in LLMs for knowledge graph entity typing (KGET). Unlike existing probing benchmarks that test factual recall, HERTy-Wiki evaluates whether models can select the most specific valid type from limited contextual evidence, reflecting realistic Wikidata scenarios, where editors often work with incomplete or noisy information. HERTy-Wiki comprises 8,767 multiple-choice questions derived from 3,776 Wikidata entities across five domains, with an optional multimodal extension. Each question requires models to discriminate between semantically related types within the same subclass hierarchy. We evaluate several state-of-the-art, reasoning-oriented LLMs under zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought prompting settings and compare them against a no-context baseline to quantify model reliance on memorised priors. Across models, macro-F1 scores remain around 0.50–0.60, with only modest improvements over the no-context baseline. Our analysis indicates that the emerging hierarchical reasoning abilities of models are overshadowed by strong dependence on memorised priors. These findings highlight fundamental challenges in using LLMs for reasoning in knowledge engineering pipelines, particularly in rapidly evolving or specialised domains with limited pre-training coverage. Title: A method for constructing a domain-specific large language model for aircraft carrier air-hub operation parsing; [面向舰载航空枢纽作业解析的领域 大模型构建方法]
Source title: Chinese Journal of Ship Research
Abstract: ［Objective］Aircraft carrier air-hub operation parsing is a typical domain-specific structured understanding task in carrier-based aviation scenarios. Its source data are primarily derived from unstructured mission logs, command messages, and support reports, and are characterized by strong temporal dependencies, complex spatiotemporal constraints, dense domain-specific terminology, and tight coupling among aircraft status, resource allocation, and operational phases. These characteristics make automatic parsing prone to errors, including omission of critical information, and structural inconsistency. Although cloud-based large language models (LLMs) offer a feasible solution due to their extensive prior knowledge and strong generative capabilities, their high computational cost and deployment requirements limit their applicability in highly resourceconstrained carrier-side environments. In contrast, locally deployable LLMs are more suitable for sensitive operational scenarios, yet their domain-specific parsing capability remains insufficient. This study aims to construct a deployable domain-specific large language model for aircraft carrier air-hub operation parsing, with the goal of improving parsing accuracy, reliability, and consistency under local deployment constraints. ［Method］We propose a domain-specific large language model construction method for carrier air-hub operation parsing, termed the carrier air-hub operation parsing large model (CAOP). The proposed framework consists of two tightly coupled stages, namely high-dimensional knowledge distillation during training and collaborative verification during inference. In the training stage, a cloud-based teacher model is employed to provide structured supervision across six key information dimensions, including entity recognition, relation extraction, statistical information extraction, predictive information extraction, joint semantic parsing of textual and numerical data, and abnormal event cue extraction. The outputs across these dimensions are further aligned and fused to construct transferable supervision signals, enabling the distillation of domain-specific parsing capabilities from the teacher model into a locally deployable student model via parameter-efficient optimization. In the inference stage, a carrier aviation operation knowledge base and a case-based retrieval mechanism are introduced to provide external evidence and similar historical instances. Based on these resources, collaborative verification is performed on candidate outputs by enforcing both evidence consistency and structural constraints, thereby reducing hallucinations, minimizing redundancy, and correcting inconsistent information fields. ［Results］Under the experimental settings adopted in this study, the proposed method improves the average score of the locally deployed Qwen3-32B model on carrier air-hub operation parsing from 13.3 to 18.4, yielding an absolute gain of 5.1 points and a relative improvement of approximately 38.3%. The resulting performance not only surpasses that of the compared cloud-based models but also approaches expert-level evaluation. The improvements are primarily reflected in more complete information field extraction, stronger evidence alignment, and enhanced structural consistency of the final parsing results.［Conclusion］The results demonstrate that the proposed CAOP framework significantly improves the accuracy, reliability, and consistency of carrier air-hub operation parsing under local deployment constraints. It provides a robust and trustworthy structured data foundation for downstream tasks, including automatic scheduling generation, conflict detection, and optimization solving. © 2026, Editorial Department of Chinese Journal of Ship Research. Title: Performance evaluation of large language models for automated knowledge graph generation
Source title: Machine Learning with Applications
Abstract: Cloud systems generate large and heterogeneous raw data logs containing information related to infrastructure, application, and security. Transforming these logs into RDF triples enables their integration into knowledge graphs, improving interpretability, root-cause analysis, and cross-service reasoning. Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a promising approach to automate RDF knowledge graph generation. However, their effectiveness on complex cloud logs remains largely unexplored. In this paper, we evaluate multiple LLM architectures and prompting strategies for automated RDF extraction using a controlled framework with two pipelines for systematically processing semi-structured log data. The extraction pipeline integrates multiple LLMs to identify relevant entities and relationships, automatically generating subject-predicate-object triples. These outputs are evaluated using a dedicated validation pipeline with both syntactic and semantic metrics to assess accuracy, completeness, and quality. Due to the lack of public ground-truth datasets, we created a reference Log-to-KG dataset from OpenStack logs using manual annotation and ontology-driven methods, enabling objective baseline. Few-Shot learning achieved the best overall performance in our evaluation, with LLaMA achieving a 99.35% F1 score and 100% valid RDF output while Qwen, NuExtract, and Gemma also perform well under Few-Shot prompting, with Chain-of-Thought approaches maintaining similar accuracy. One-Shot prompting offers a lighter but effective alternative, while Zero-Shot and strategies such as Single-Prompt Tree-of-Thought, and Generate-Multiple-Then-Vote showed consistently lower performance. The top-performing LLMs, LLaMA and Qwen, with One-Shot and Few-Shot prompting were evaluated on a different dataset, to assess transferability, performance stability and efficiency in terms of latency, token generation, and GPU memory usage. Our work highlights the importance of contextual examples and prompt design for accurate RDF extraction and reveal model-specific limitations across LLM architectures offering practical guidelines and a foundation for future knowledge graphs extraction from unstructured data research. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Huang Z.; Yang W.; Li X.; Bai Q.
Title: Multi-source knowledge graph construction through LLM-assisted incremental fusion
Source title: Intelligent Systems with Applications
Abstract: Real-world data often originates from multiple heterogeneous sources describing the same entities. When multiple sources target the same domain, they produce overlapping and conflicting information requiring reconciliation. Traditional approaches rely on rule-based entity matching that struggles with semantic variations, or employ late fusion at query time leading to redundancy and unresolved conflicts. This paper presents a general framework for constructing unified knowledge graphs through entity-level early fusion. We propose a multi-agent incremental fusion pipeline designed to handle diverse data formats. We implement the framework for three data types: structured databases (MySQL), semi-structured data (JSON), and unstructured text. The core innovation is a dual-support conflict detection mechanism combining rule-based text similarity with structure-based graph topology, followed by large language model (LLM)-assisted resolution. We evaluate the framework using a music domain case study integrating four sources (Chinook, Spotify, MusicBrainz, Wikipedia), creating overlaps and property conflicts. Our benchmark comprises 50 questions across five reasoning categories, evaluated against two baselines: multi-agent late fusion retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and independent GraphRAG. Results demonstrate clear advantages: 72.1% win rate in qualitative evaluation, near-perfect faithfulness (0.955) and context precision (0.932), 18.9% improvement in context recall (0.876 vs 0.737), and 64.6% improvement in multi-hop reasoning context recall (0.874 vs 0.531). These findings validate that entity-level fusion during graph construction provides stronger foundations for retrieval-augmented generation compared to query-time fusion, and the framework is designed to be generalizable to other domains requiring multi-source integration. © 2026 The Authors

The model embodies key soft computing principles—flexibility, adaptability, and approximate reasoning—by employing a multi-scale feature fusion mechanism, relation-aware graph attention, and a global correspondence alignment module for overlapping relation disambiguation. Built upon pre-trained language models, DCGAT-RE introduces an adaptive gating mechanism to fuse syntactic and semantic cues while jointly optimizing entity recognition and relation prediction. Experiments on multiple Chinese medical benchmarks (CMeIE, CMeIE-V2, and DiaKG) demonstrate that DCGAT-RE achieves superior performance with an F1-score of 77.1%, surpassing strong baselines such as ERNIE-Health by over 11%. Title: Knowledge graph construction for power grid fault handling based on prompt learning and LoRA fine-tuning

Abstract: In complex and diverse power grid fault scenarios, constructing a systematic fault handling knowledge system is an effective approach to enhancing the intelligence of fault handling. Title: LiveGraph: A Compound AI System for Evolving Knowledge Graph Construction from Streaming Data

Abstract: Constructing knowledge graphs from streaming data requires coordinating LLMs, embedding models, graph databases, and domain adapters - yet existing systems compose these components through ad-hoc interfaces, making them brittle to component changes and opaque to debugging. Title: LLM-based domain-specific knowledge graph construction and hybrid retrieval-augmented generation

Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) empowered by large language models is emerging as a promising approach for industrial knowledge analysis and decision support. Title: Comparative Analysis of Multi-Agent Architectures for Entity Relationship Classification

Title: TriRE: Three-Stage Reflection for Training-Free Relation Extraction

Abstract: We study TriRE (Three-Stage Reflection for Relation Extraction), a training-free relation extraction method for black-box LLM text APIs. Title: How can the integration of AI large language models and knowledge graph enhance fault diagnosis? A systematic literature review
Source title: Applied Soft Computing
Abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Knowledge Graphs (KGs) represents an emerging approach to improving fault diagnosis in industrial settings. Traditional fault diagnosis methods—including model-based, signal-based, and rule-based approaches—face persistent challenges in managing complex data, adapting to new failures, and ensuring reasoning accuracy. This systematic literature review evaluates 37 relevant studies to examine how the synergy between LLMs and KGs can mitigate these limitations. The review identifies two primary paradigms: LLM-augmented KGs, which automate the extraction of entities and relationships from unstructured industrial text, and KG-enhanced LLMs (GraphRAG), which ground model reasoning in structured causal paths to reduce hallucinations. While the integrated use of these technologies is a growing research trend, particularly with a peak of 11 papers published in 2025, the field remains in its early stages. Current research is heavily concentrated on rotating machinery, steel manufacturing, and computer numerical control (CNC) equipment, with significant gaps in industry coverage, multilingual support (beyond English and Chinese), and advanced evaluation metrics. Furthermore, many existing systems lack the explainability required for engineers to interpret reasoning routes in high-stakes environments. This study suggests that future research should focus on expanding diagnostic frameworks to specialized industries, improving domain-specific adaptations, and enhancing interpretability through interactive visualization and structured reasoning. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Deep Semantic Linking of Scientific Knowledge: An Agentic AI Framework for Knowledge Graph Construction
Source title: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
Abstract: The foundation of scientific research is the comprehensive analysis of existing literature. However, the exponential growth of published research leaves scientists increasingly overwhelmed, making it difficult to maintain a complete overview of the state-of-the-art or to discover hidden synergies between studies. To enable true machine-assisted exploration and verification, scholarly literature must be transformed from isolated documents into deeply interlinked, machine-readable structures. Title: LLM-Driven Multimodal Knowledge Graph Construction for Industrial Process with Prompt Optimization and Fuzzy RAG
Source title: IEEE Transactions on Fuzzy Systems
Abstract: The industrial flotation process involves multimodal data and cross-procedural knowledge, presenting significant challenges for knowledge system management and traditional knowledge graph (KG) construction methods. This study develops a large language model (LLM)-driven framework to construct a domain-specific multimodal KG. The flotation knowledge tree ontology is designed as the structural backbone of the KG to organize multilevel operations and interactions while integrating heterogeneous flotation data. To enhance the LLM's domain adaptability, adaptive prompt optimization is proposed to iteratively refine the extraction template with flotation-specific examples and performance feedback, enabling more accurate triple extraction. In addition, a fuzzy information entropy-driven retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) method is proposed, leveraging fuzzy logic to assign weights to key terms and numerical contexts to preserve causal relationships and semantic integrity under data uncertainty. Furthermore, we established a two-stage LLM-driven pipeline to generate initial triples using a low-rank adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuned lightweight LLM with the optimized prompt and fuzzy RAG context, followed by refinement with a large-scale LLM for precision and ontology alignment. Validated triples are mapped onto the flotation knowledge tree to form a structured, high-quality KG with minimal manual intervention. Title: Bi-term association based on fuzzy logic
Source title: Array
Abstract: Traditional Boolean search strategies identify co-occurrence but fail to capture semantic relationships. Current relation extraction (RE) frameworks, which rely on domain-specific training, struggle with adaptability to emerging research topics. Bi-term associations are defined as contextually grounded relationships that extend co-occurrence analysis while avoiding the data annotation requirements of traditional RE. Key contributions include: a fuzzy logic framework for graded membership assignment to capture uncertainty and relationship strength, design of complex fuzzy rules within a lightweight zero-shot LLM, and detailed demonstration of four conceptual case studies in diverse fields, ranging from simple to complex rule design. Title: ID-GraphRAG: An Incremental Construction Framework of Document-Level Retrieval-Augmented Knowledge Graphs with Multi-agent Verification
Source title: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
Abstract: The rapid development of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval Enhanced Generative (RAG) technologies is profoundly transforming the paradigm of knowledge graph (KGs) construction. Abstract: With the continuous expansion of industrial systems, multisource and heterogeneous industrial data have increased rapidly, making the construction of a structured industrial knowledge system a core requirement in the industrial domain. Title: Constraint-Guided In-Context Learning for Domain-Specific Triplet Extraction

Abstract: The automation of high-quality knowledge graph construction hinges on the precise extraction of relational triplets from unstructured text. While large language models (LLMs) offer potential solutions, current approaches remain limited in specialized domains due to their reliance on manual annotation and model fine-tuning. Crucially, the absence of explicit constraints on knowledge reasoning introduces significant uncertainty and errors in domain-specific triplet extraction. To address these gaps, this study proposes OntoP2KG, a novel framework integrating domain ontology constraints with structured prompt engineering. The method first identifies domain-subdomain attributes of input text, retrieves relevant concepts from ontologies and few-shot examples, and constructs a knowledge-enriched context. Subsequently, through structured prompts, the LLM is guided to perform accurate triplet extraction, followed by redundancy resolution based on graph embedding similarity and rule matching. Abstract: Cantonese opera, as a national intangible cultural heritage, contains rich information on roles, schools, and lineages in its scripts and biographies of performers. However, for a long time, related research has mainly relied on manual textual research, making it difficult to systematically reveal the lineage at the large-scale textual level. Title: MSKGCF: A Framework for Multimodal Scientific Knowledge Graph Construction and Fusion
Source title: Proceedings of the International Conference on Computer Supported Cooperative Work in Design, CSCWD
Abstract: Scientific Knowledge Graphs (SKGs) are foundational for automated discovery and reasoning. However, their construction faces critical hurdles due to the heterogeneity of scientific literature, where essential information is fragmented across complex text and unstructured visual modalities like figures and tables. Furthermore, the rapid growth of publications makes continuous updates necessary, as rebuilding from scratch is costly. To address this, we propose MSKGCF, a novel framework for Multimodal Scientific Knowledge Graph Construction and Fusion. MSKGCF adopts a two-stage extraction strategy, first entity recognition, then relation classification, driven by a general-purpose Teacher LLM (GPT-4o) to capture information across text and visual modalities. Furthermore, we introduce a logic-based fusion mechanism to integrate disparate sub-graphs via LLM-based conflict resolution, ensuring scalability. Experiments show that MSKGCF outperforms existing methods in extraction accuracy. Title: Autonomous construction of crop pest and disease knowledge graphs at scale via LLM-driven expert modeling
Source title: Computers and Electronics in Agriculture
Abstract: Crop pests and diseases pose a serious threat to global food security, which create an urgent need for rapid and accurate plant protection strategies. Much of the domain knowledge required for such intervention, however, remains scattered across heterogeneous and largely unstructured literature. This fragmentation limits the effective use of agricultural data in intelligent diagnosis and decision support, and it has increased the demand for high quality domain specific knowledge graphs. Existing approaches to agricultural knowledge graph construction still rely heavily on manual or partially automated curation, which restricts the efficient use of unstructured multi-source data and slows the incorporation of updated domain knowledge. To address these limitations, this study presents CropKG, an autonomous AI driven framework for reconstructing the knowledge engineering workflow in agricultural protection. Unlike conventional semi-automated approaches, CropKG integrates automated prompt engineering with expert oriented role modeling. By encoding agronomic reasoning patterns and combining them with bottom-up ontology induction, the framework supports autonomous extraction of complex entity relations from long agricultural documents while reducing unsupported generation in large language models. The effectiveness of the framework is demonstrated through the construction of a large-scale domain knowledge graph containing more than 17,000 nodes. Experimental results show that CropKG achieves an F1 score above 90% in entity and relation extraction and outperforms strong universal extraction baselines. The framework also supports decision-oriented applications by enabling traceable and evidence constrained retrieval of pest control knowledge. These results indicate that autonomous knowledge graph construction provides a practical path from raw agricultural text to structured and actionable intelligence for precision plant protection. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Structure Shapes the Future of DataxLLM Systems: Retrieval, Structuring, and Reasoning
Source title: Proceedings of the ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have transformed AI, yet they remain fundamentally limited by hallucination, unverifiable reasoning, and shallow evidence grounding. We argue that structure mining-rooted in decades of KDD research on taxonomy induction, ontology design, entity typing, and knowledge graph construction-is the key to overcoming these limitations. This tutorial presents a unified vision in which structuring serves as the enabling foundation for three pillars of next-generation LLM systems: (1) Structured Retrieval, where organizing corpora into ontology-guided multidimensional representations enables SQL-like queries that achieve substantially more precise and complete retrieval than similarity-based approaches; (2) Structured Reasoning, where grounding each inference step in typed, graph-structured evidence transforms opaque generation into auditable, verifiable reasoning chains; and (3) Structured Agent Memory, where multi-dimensional memory architectures bridge external corpus knowledge and experiential agent knowledge through a mutually enriching dual-memory design. Across all three pillars, we highlight how the cooperative interplay between classical KDD techniques and modern LLMs-where KDD defines structural schemas and quality constraints while LLMs execute flexible extraction and reasoning-creates systems that are more reliable, interpretable, and faithful. The tutorial covers both foundational methods and the latest advances (2024 - 2026), and concludes with open problems and future research directions at the intersection of data mining and LLMs. © 2026 Owner/Author.

Title: A knowledge-enhanced dual-perspective reasoning encoding framework that integrates large language models

Abstract: Currently, joint extraction models have become the mainstream solution for entity-relation extraction tasks and have achieved remarkable results in general domains. Title: From Memorization to Discovery: A Novel Benchmark for Relational Triple Extraction
Source title: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
Abstract: Relational Triple Extraction (RTE) mines factual knowledge components as relational triples from unstructured text. Title: From Graph to Text and Back: Semantic Fidelity in Automated Industrial Knowledge Graphs
Source title: Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
Abstract: Knowledge Graphs (KGs) are the backbone of reliable industrial data strategies, yet verbalizing them with Large Language Models (LLMs) often leads to unacceptable risks for high-stakes applications, such as hallucinations or omitted relations. Experiments confirm that our automated round-trip consistency score correlates strongly with expert judgment, effectively acting as a scalable proxy for human review. Furthermore, we show that standard LLMs can bootstrap their own KG-extraction and generation capabilities by fine-tuning on this trusted synthetic data. Title: SCoRE: Streamlined corpus-based relation extraction using multi-label contrastive learning and Bayesian kNN

Abstract: The growing demand for efficient knowledge graph (KG) enrichment leveraging external corpora has intensified interest in relation extraction (RE), particularly under low-supervision settings. Authors: Huang H.; Hong Z.
Title: Extract, Align, Reflect: An LLM-Based Framework for Knowledge Graph Construction
Source title: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
Abstract: Automated Knowledge Graph Construction (KGC) from natural language text is a pivotal task for achieving intelligent machine cognition and reasoning. With the rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs), researchers have extensively explored direct generation of entity-relation triplets via zero-shot or few-shot prompting, significantly reducing the reliance on manual annotation and rule-based engineering inherent in traditional pipeline methods. However, in real-world open-domain scenarios, existing LLM-driven KGC approaches still face two critical challenges: First, the schema dependency bottleneck. To ensure structural validity, most methods explicitly inject target schemas into prompts. When dealing with large-scale or complex relation sets, this approach is constrained by the context window limit and fails to adapt to dynamic knowledge systems. Second, the hallucination-induced noise. The inherent probabilistic nature of LLMs often leads to redundant entities and unreliable relationships that lack textual support or factual consistency, even after formal alignment. To address these issues, we propose EAR, a three-phase KGC framework comprising Extract, Align, and Reflect. Built upon open information extraction, EAR enhances semantic consistency and factual faithfulness through a dedicated schema alignment mechanism and a triple reflection module. Extensive experiments on multiple public benchmarks demonstrate that EAR significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods. Specifically, EAR achieves higher F1 scores in schema-constrained settings and generates structurally accurate, low-redundancy knowledge in schema-free environments. Compared to recent LLM-driven KGC works, EAR exhibits superior versatility and scalability while effectively mitigating the schema-injection bottleneck and generation noise. This work provides a systematic pathway for building high-quality, interpretable autonomous knowledge engineering systems. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: Diagnosing public EV charging deficits via LLM-KG analysis of citizen complaints in Wuhan

The knowledge graph links problem types, responsible entities, geographic locations, and temporal references. The results show that fire safety hazards, installation barriers, and absence of ancillary facilities account for 79.53% of problem entities. Negative sentiment exceeds 69% in every category. Title: Counterfactual-based Cognitive Alignment In-Context Learning for Relation Extraction

Title: SPKG: A Two-Stage Structured Prompting Framework for Knowledge Graph Construction
Source title: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have recently shown strong potential in knowledge graph (KG) construction due to their advanced text understanding capabilities. However, existing approaches based on plain-text prompting struggle to express complex and fine-grained extraction constraints, limiting the model’s ability to accurately interpret task requirements. At the content level, prompts are organized into functional components, including task instructions, domain knowledge, output specifications, few-shot examples, and input text, enabling more precise semantic parsing. At the form level, explicit structural delimiters (e.g., XML or JSON) are employed to clearly separate components, improving the model’s ability to follow complex instructions and constraints. Title: Decomposing Complexity: A Difficulty-Aware Multi-agent Framework for Open-Domain Knowledge Graph Construction
Source title: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
Abstract: Knowledge graphs (KGs) connect information and reveal hidden relationships in various domains. Our quantitative analysis reveals that these tasks are far more difficult than commonly perceived, causing even frontier larger language models (LLMs) to lack consistent reliability. This finding indicates that an end-to-end approach relying on simple, direct prompting for these tasks is insufficient to build robust systems. In this paper, we propose a difficulty-aware multi-agent framework (DAMA), which tackles the difficulty of KG construction through strategic decomposition. DAMA deconstructs these key tasks into more tractable sub-tasks, allowing a team of diverse agents to solve them collaboratively. This decomposition tailors each agent’s task space, which reduces the required context length and mitigates semantic reasoning demands. For a more comprehensive evaluation of factual correctness, we also introduce two novel metrics: contradiction rate (CR) and substantive information density (SID). Title: Large Language Model-Driven Knowledge Graph Construction and Restoration Measure Decision Support for Sustainable Mine Ecological Restoration
Source title: Sustainability (Switzerland)
Abstract: Mine ecological restoration involves multiple tasks, including ecological problem identification, restoration measure selection, and restoration effect evaluation. Relevant knowledge is widely scattered across academic literature and policy and regulatory documents, making it difficult to directly support structured queries, knowledge association, and measure screening. To address the insufficient organization of knowledge in mine ecological restoration and the unstable quality of triples extracted by large language models, this study proposes a large language model-driven workflow for knowledge graph construction and restoration measure decision support in mine ecological restoration. First, a weak ontology schema containing eight entity types and eight relation types was constructed, and a manually annotated dataset was developed based on 30 papers on mine ecological restoration. Second, multiple large language models were compared on the triple extraction task, and Kimi, which achieved the best overall performance, was selected for large-scale knowledge extraction. On this basis, a weak-ontology-guided triple quality control method, named WOTQC, was proposed to check the structural consistency of candidate triples in terms of entity type, relation type, relation direction, and entity orientation. DeepSeek was then introduced to perform verification based on original textual evidence. Subsequently, entity normalization and relation aggregation were conducted on the verified triples to construct a knowledge graph for mine ecological restoration. Path mining, restoration measure decision support, and external case validation were further performed around the “ecological problem–restoration measure–restoration effect” path. The experimental results show that Kimi-based initial extraction achieved an F1 score of 0.7286. After WOTQC processing, the F1 score increased to 0.7561, and after DeepSeek-based evidence verification, it further improved to 0.7862. The external case validation shows that the integrated ranking method achieved 1.00 under both strict Hit@3 and strict Hit@5, with a path explanation coverage@5 of 0.7500. Title: Forecasting Enterprise Performance in the IC Industry: A Framework Combining Evolutionary Event Graphs and Supply Chain Propagation
Source title: Pacific Asia Conference on Information Systems
Abstract: As geopolitical tensions and supply chain disruptions intensify, integrated circuit (IC) enterprises face unprecedented uncertainty, making accurate performance prediction critical and challenging. Existing approaches predominantly rely on historical financial time series and struggle to capture exogenous shocks and their cascading effects across firms. This study proposes EvoChain, a predictive framework that integrates evolutionary event graphs (EEGs) with supply chain network structure for firm-level performance forecasting. EvoChain extracts EEGs from IC industry news using NER and large language model–based relation extraction, and adopts a layered heterogeneous graph design: a GCN encodes each firm's local EEG subgraph into an event-evolution embedding, which then serves as the node feature for a GAT over supply chain network. An attention-based gating mechanism integrates these representations with historical financial sequences for jointly predicting four financial metrics. Title: NERLLM: Efficient integration of local NER models and large language models for named entity recognition
Source title: Expert Systems with Applications
Abstract: Named Entity Recognition (NER) is a core primitive for information extraction and knowledge graph construction in data and knowledge engineering systems. Fine-tuned local NER models are typically fast and precise in-domain, but may degrade when facing language polysemy or emerging entities. In contrast, large language models (LLMs) offer broader contextual reasoning, but applying them directly to NER tasks often yields low precision. While recent hybrid solutions have explored combining local NER models with LLMs, they still face two limitations: routing is typically driven by heuristic confidence signals, which can limit their ability to consistently prioritize genuine prediction errors under strict API cost constraints; and verification is predominantly used in a rejection-oriented manner, rather than enabling structured correction of partially correct spans. To address these limitations, we propose NERLLM, a cost-conscious pipeline that selectively routes low-confidence spans from a local NER model to an LLM for verification and correction. NERLLM learns a lightweight span-level confidence scorer from model outputs and dataset statistics, and uses a multi-stage rechecking pipeline to correct labels, boundaries and resolve conflicts with optional secondary verification. Experiments on three benchmark datasets spanning news and social media show that NERLLM improves micro-F1 over the evaluated standalone local NER models and direct LLM prompting baselines, while reducing unnecessary LLM usage through selective rechecking.
